question: Your team moved contract extraction from JSON in Claude's text replies to an extraction tool whose input parameters are the contract JSON schema. A week later, the downstream contract database still rejects about 2% of the records because of JSON syntax errors. The logs show that every Claude response for these records contains a tool_use block whose input matches the schema. What is the most likely cause of the rejected records?

options.text: The request sets tool_choice to "any" instead of forcing the extraction tool, so Claude may write the contract fields in a syntax that is not valid JSON.
options.reason: With tool_choice "any" Claude must still call a tool, and the logs show a schema-matching tool_use block, so this setting cannot explain the syntax errors.

options.text: The pipeline still parses JSON out of the text content of each response instead of reading the input of the tool_use block.
options.reason: Tool use with a JSON schema eliminates JSON syntax errors in the tool_use input, so syntax errors that remain point to code that still parses the text reply.

options.text: The schema has no "other" enum value with a detail string, so contract types outside the enum list produce malformed JSON in the tool input.
options.reason: The guide uses "other" plus a detail string for extensible categorization, not to prevent syntax errors, which tool use with a JSON schema already eliminates.

options.text: The schema marks several fields as optional, so Claude leaves out brackets and quotes in the tool input when a source contract lacks that information.
options.reason: The guide makes fields optional (nullable) to prevent fabricated values when information is missing, and tool use with a schema eliminates syntax errors regardless of which fields are optional.
